cefrAlignment: Matches the C1 grammatical accuracy descriptor (consistently maintains a high degree of accuracy; errors are rare and hard to spot) by training learners to self-monitor and correct; the error types and the corrected texts suit C1.
examFidelity: Band-descriptor references now follow the May 2023 public IELTS descriptors, the TOEFL Academic Discussion (10 minutes) and TOEIC (30 minutes) references match exams.ts, and every error-correction item has an unambiguous error and complete accepted corrections (the 14 errors in the editing task were counted and confirmed).
fixes: Replaced old band-descriptor wording ('good control') with the 2023 text: 'generally well controlled', 'error-free sentences are frequent' and, at band 8, 'the majority of sentences are error-free'
Softened unverifiable frequency claims ('the errors that most often…', 'Most C1 writers…') to 'common errors that can…' and 'Many C1 writers…'
Edited model paragraph: restored 'Nowadays', which was silently changed to 'Today' although it was not an error
Dangling-modifier explanation: removed the suggested correction 'Having finished the report, I saw the computer crash', which changes the meaning; the explanation now says what the error implies
Rubric item relabelled from Lexical resource to Grammatical range and accuracy (infinitive and article errors are grammar) and made specific
Model answer uses 'doesn't' (the minimal correction, and natural in a TOEFL post), and the corrections list notes 'or does not'
openConcerns: The paragraph-editing task is checked by comparison with the model only; learners who fix an error differently (for example, a full stop instead of 'and' for a comma splice) need to judge for themselves whether their fix is acceptable
learnerOutcome: A learner can run a quick three-pass check (verbs, nouns, sentence boundaries) and reliably fix agreement, article, uncountable-noun, word-form, comma-splice and fragment errors in their own exam writing.
